intro: Buddhists around the world know the story of the Buddha's life. They see it painted on temple walls, acted out at festivals and told to children. Pilgrims still visit the places where they believe it happened.

In this unit you will follow that story as the texts tell it. You will read about Lumbini, the Four Sights, the Great Going Forth and the awakening. Then you will follow the Buddha's teaching life, the first nuns, and his last journey.

You will also learn to ask where each part comes from. Some details are in the oldest suttas. Others come from later life stories. By the end, you will be able to retell the life and name the texts behind it.
bigQuestion: How do the Buddhist texts tell the Buddha's life, and why do the tellings differ?

timeline.t: Many scholars date the Buddha's birth near here; tradition gives 624 or 563 BCE.
Tradition says Siddhartha is born in the garden at Lumbini.
The Four Sights and the Great Going Forth.
Years with teachers and hard fasting, then the middle way.
Buddhists believe he awakens under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.
The first sermon in the Deer Park at Sarnath (Samyutta Nikaya 56.11).
Mahapajapati and other women become the first nuns (Cullavagga 10).
The Buddha dies at Kushinagar (Digha Nikaya 16).
King Ashoka sets up a pillar at Lumbini.
Ashvaghosha writes the Buddhacarita (scholars' dating: 1st–2nd century).

words.d: the garden in today's Nepal where tradition says the Buddha was born
an old man, a sick man, a dead man and a holy man, which led Siddhartha to leave home
a person who gives up comforts to seek spiritual truth
"Acts of the Buddha," a long Sanskrit poem about his life by Ashvaghosha
the path between too much comfort and too much hardship
in Buddhism, seeing the truth about life fully; also called enlightenment
the Deer Park near Varanasi where the Buddha gave his first sermon
the Buddhist community, especially monks and nuns
the ceremony that makes someone a monk or nun
in Buddhism, the end of suffering (Pali: nibbana)
a journey to a holy place

test.q: Who were the Buddha's parents, says tradition?
test.why: Tradition names King Suddhodana and Queen Maya.

test.q: What did Maya dream about, say the life stories?
test.why: The stories say she dreamed of a white elephant.

test.q: Which ancient object names Lumbini as the birthplace?
test.why: Ashoka's pillar inscription names Lumbini as the birthplace.

test.q: Which text tells the Four Sights about Vipassi?
test.why: Digha Nikaya 14 tells the pattern about the earlier Buddha Vipassi.
Kanthaka was the white horse of the Great Going Forth.

test.q: In Majjhima Nikaya 26, how does he leave home?
test.why: This older sutta has no midnight ride; his parents weep.

test.q: What did Siddhartha find after years of fasting?
test.why: He found hard fasting did not work and chose the middle way.

test.q: What does the earth-touching gesture remember?
choices: calling the earth to witness against Mara
test.why: The stories say he touched the earth when Mara challenged him.
The first sermon was in the Deer Park at Sarnath.
Buddhists take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma and Sangha.

test.q: Who led the first women to become nuns?
test.why: The Vinaya says Mahapajapati led the first nuns.

test.q: What did the Buddha ask Kisa Gotami to find?
choices: a leaf from the Bodhi tree
a mustard seed from a house with no death
test.why: Her search taught her that every family knows loss.

test.q: Where did the Buddha die, says Digha Nikaya 16?
test.why: The Mahaparinibbana Sutta places his death near Kushinagar.

choices: a later poem telling the Buddha's whole life
test.why: Ashvaghosha's Buddhacarita tells the full life, centuries after the Buddha.

test.q: Which is one of the four pilgrimage places?
test.why: The four places are Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar.

write.prompt: The Great Going Forth is told two ways. Compare the midnight ride in the later life stories with Majjhima Nikaya 26. Cite both, explain what each says, and suggest why Buddhists value each telling.
tips: Name each text you cite, with its number.
Say "the story says" or "Buddhists believe" for each belief.
Compare the tellings; do not judge which is true.
Use unit words like ascetic, Sangha and middle way.
